testPolicy.text: Texas A&M University is test optional and will not require ACT or SAT scores for freshman applicants; students with scores are encouraged to send them through the testing agency, and the highest total score from a single test date is considered. CDS C8A for fall 2027 applicants: not required, but considered if submitted.

cost.totalIncludes: CDS section G for the full 2026-27 academic year, first-year column: tuition + required fees + food and housing on campus (housing 8,844 + food 4,100), plus G5 books and supplies, transportation and other expenses. No total is published: the financial aid office directs students to a tuition calculator.

inState.note: all-undergraduate column tuition 8,908; tuition varies by major

aidPromise.text: Aggie Assurance: for students whose family income is $60,000 or less, tuition and fees are covered by grants and/or scholarships (fees added from fall 2023); students with family income above $60,000 and up to $130,000 can receive tuition support grants of $500 to $1,500 (College Station only).

deadlines.regular: December 1 (fall, College Station; documents by December 15; decisions roll from September for top 10% applicants and from October for holistic review)

facts.text: Texas residents in the top 10 percent of their graduating class are automatically admitted to Texas A&M; decisions for them start in September.
Texas A&M admitted 32,531 of 62,967 first-year applicants for fall 2025, including 26,620 of 49,156 Texans and 4,489 of 10,882 out-of-state applicants.
Engineering applicants, including automatic top-10-percent admits, are reviewed separately for placement into General Engineering.
Families earning $60,000 or less have tuition and fees covered under Aggie Assurance.
Testing is optional: the ACT or SAT is not required, and the highest total from a single test date is used if sent.
In 2026-27 a non-resident pays 36,877 in first-year tuition against 8,886 for a Texan, plus 3,970 in required fees.

notes: Cycle from the HTML CDS 2025-26 C1 (31,337 + 31,630 = 62,967 applied; 16,375 + 16,156 = 32,531 admitted; 6,334 + 6,150 = 12,484 enrolled, of which 1,702 part-time). The abpa.tamu.edu site returns 404 to a bare curl user agent and works with a browser user agent. No waiting list (C2). C22 says Early Action Yes with 'October 15th' and dates N/A, but the admissions page shows October 15 as the spring deadline and December 1 as the fall deadline with rolling decisions; no EA plan is recorded for fall. C12 GPA N/A. No official cost-of-attendance table found (tuition calculator only); the affordability page still quotes a 2024-25 estimate of about 29,684 in-state. No official fall 2026 class numbers recorded.
